input.summary: Blocked: the two criteria contradict each other, so I wrote no tests or stubs. C-7d08730c requires slugify("Hello World", keep_case=True) to return "Hello-World", which has uppercase letters. C-cdceffb7 requires the slug for that same call to contain no uppercase letter. No implementation can satisfy both. The "Slugs are always lowercase" requirement also says "no exceptions" for every combination of arguments, which conflicts with the "Case preservation" requirement. A product owner needs to decide which one wins.

questions.title: Which requirement wins: case preservation or always-lowercase?
questions.context: Case preservation says slugify("Hello World", keep_case=True) == "Hello-World". 'Slugs are always lowercase' says the slug for that same call has no uppercase letter, for every argument combination with no exceptions. Both scenarios use the identical call, so they cannot both pass.
options: Keep case preservation; remove or amend the 'always lowercase' requirement (e.g. lowercase only when keep_case=False)
Keep always-lowercase; drop the keep_case feature or change its expected output
Redefine keep_case so it preserves case only in some narrower way (specify how)
